name: gas_engine_rankine_bottoming
title: Gas engine with Rankine bottoming cycle (positive-displacement expander)
summary: Steady-state model of a spark-ignition engine whose exhaust gas feeds a recovery boiler (effectiveness 0.8) and a bottoming Rankine cycle on Water with positive-displacement expander and pump: engine states from intake to exhaust, boiler/expander/condenser/pump states, steam flow, Rankine and global efficiencies.

authors: ULiege MSTh course (J. Lebrun, V. Lemort, S. Bertagnolio)
origin.course: ULiege MSTh, machines et systemes thermiques, repetition TP 12 (exercise 8)

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solution of MSTH-SB-R12-EX8.EES with compare_solution.py: '99 common variables, 5 differ (rtol=0.001)'. The 5 are the constant Air entropy reference offset (s_2, 0.32) and the cpbar mean specific heats with the variables that follow them (cp_p_67, cp_p_78, C_3, A_soupapes, 1.3-1.7e-3, ideal-gas species data EES vs CoolProp); all 94 others agree to <= 9.7e-4.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file (work reference ees_variables.csv)
verification.notes: The s_2 deviation is a constant entropy reference-state offset of Air (EES ideal-gas Air vs CoolProp pseudo-pure Air); it cancels in the isentropic inversion (T_3, v_3 agree to 5e-4). Needs the shipped .initials (EES guesses): the flame temperature sits inside the cpbar calls and default guesses diverge.
